Shared laws, commands and teaching applying to all within the stated audience or conditions. General does not remove covenant, historical, priestly or household limits. Read the existing Transformed, Fulfilled, Unchanged, Everlasting and other classifications alongside each entry.

Some source records still need their audience resolved. These are explicitly marked audience review pending; their provisional filing here is not a claim that they apply universally. Passage groups may contain both shared teaching and personal directions.

General · Personal · Instructions overview

3,869 study records in this view. Entries can overlap; this is not a count of distinct biblical commands. Ordered by the first source book, chapter and verse.

The source wording follows the Saints Greek-English text: the Septuagint for the Old Testament and the Greek New Testament. Headings and application notes are study summaries. Preserve the passage’s speaker, audience, conditions and grammatical form. Source alignment checked 6 November 2026; independent critical-Greek review remains in progress.

S098 · Blasphemy and Israel’s judicial penalty

Source wording · Saints Greek-English

This is the cited study context; the record does not identify a separate primary command passage.

24:10 And the son of an Israelite woman, whose father was an Egyptian man, went out among the sons of Israel. The Israelite woman’s son and an Israelite man fought in the camp.

24:11 And the Israelite woman’s son pronounced the Name and cursed, and they brought him unto Moses. His mother’s name was Shelomith daughter of Dibri, of the tribe of Dan.

24:12 And they placed him in custody, to judge him by the Lord’s command.

24:13 And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying:

24:14 Bring the one who cursed outside the camp. All who heard him shall lay their hands on his head, and the whole congregation shall stone him.

24:15 And speak unto the sons of Israel, and you shall say unto them: A man who curses God shall bear sin.

24:16 Let one who names the Lord’s name surely be put to death. Let the whole congregation of Israel stone him with stones. Whether resident foreigner or native-born, when he names the Lord’s name, let him die.

Leviticus 24:10–16

Audience: Shared instruction or study teaching. Read the original audience, conditions and existing classification before applying it.

Classification: Study context · Topical study

Topic: Justice, testimony, government and war

Original scope: Text and setting: Civil penalty

Connection to Christ: Jesus’ command to love enemies and the apostolic rejection of private vengeance govern Christian response to the ancient penalty. Christian response today: Honor God and pursue lawful protection where needed; do not execute or threaten people for blasphemy.

S101 · Jubilee, release and the land’s ownership

Source wording · Saints Greek-English

This is the cited study context; the record does not identify a separate primary command passage.

25:8 And you shall count unto yourself seven rests of years, seven years seven times; and the seven weeks of years shall be unto you forty-nine years.

25:9 And you shall make proclamation with a trumpet sound throughout your land in the seventh month, on the tenth day of the month. On the Day of Atonement you shall make proclamation with a trumpet throughout your land.

25:10 And you shall consecrate the fiftieth year, and proclaim release throughout the land unto all who dwell therein; this shall be a year of release, a signal unto you; and each one shall depart unto his possession, and each of you shall depart unto his ancestral homeland.

25:11 This is a signal of release: the fiftieth year shall be a year for you. You shall not sow, reap what grows of itself, or gather its consecrated produce.

25:12 For it is a signal of release; it shall be holy to you. You shall eat its produce from the fields.

25:13 In the year of release, at its signal, each shall return to his possession.

25:14 But if one sells property unto your neighbour, or you acquire it from your neighbour, let no man oppress his neighbour.

25:15 According to the number of years after the signal you shall acquire from your neighbour; according to the number of harvest years he shall sell to you.

25:16 As the years increase, you shall increase its purchase price; as the years decrease, you shall decrease its purchase price, for he is selling you a number of harvests.

25:17 Let no man oppress his neighbour, and you shall fear the Lord your God; I am the Lord your God.

Leviticus 25:8–17

Audience: Shared instruction or study teaching. Read the original audience, conditions and existing classification before applying it.

Classification: Study context · Topical study

Topic: Land, harvests and provision for the poor

Original scope: Text and setting: Land covenant

Connection to Christ: Jesus announces release through Isaiah in Luke 4; connecting this with Jubilee is a Christian interpretation, not a statement that he enacted every land provision. Christian response today: Practice generosity and concern for freedom without promising automatic cancellation of every modern debt or property claim.
